subject: ClearShield RFP: multi-region recovery commitments and evidence
messages:
From: Meera Rao <meera@clearshield.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: security@clearshield.com
Date: Tue, 21 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: ClearShield RFP - follow-up on DR / BCP details

Hi Grace,

Thanks again for the call earlier — ClearShield is working through the RFP checklist and we need a concise set of commitments and evidence for multi-region recovery. Specifically we need the following by COB next week:

- Target RTO and RPO for your hosted inference offering and for Dedicated deployments
- Failover sequencing (control plane, data plane, DNS, cache warm-up) and expected times per step
- Any dependencies that could extend RTO/RPO (e.g., cross-region storage, KMS key rotation)
- Recent runbook extract or warm-up checklist we can show auditors
- Pointer to SOC2 / penetration test / DR test evidence (redacted ok)

We will treat this as part of the security/compliance evaluation for our procurement committee. If you can attach a short summary and any runbook excerpts, that would be ideal.

Thanks,
Meera Rao
Director, Vendor Security
ClearShield Financial

[Attachment requested: runbook excerpt, warm-up checklist]

From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>

Hi Meera —

Appreciate the clear ask. Attached is a concise summary (Redwood_DR_Summary_20260722.pdf) that addresses each bullet; below are the highlights and timings tailored to the two deployment modes you referenced. We'll follow up with a short call to walk through any questions.

High-level commitments (summary):
- Hosted API (multi-region active/passive):
  - RTO: automated traffic switch to secondary region begins within 3-5 minutes of failover trigger; full capacity typically restored within 30 minutes as dependent services and caches warm.
  - RPO: for inference requests and control-plane metadata we maintain near-zero logical loss when customers enable cross-region replication; default logging/event retention is configurable per account.
- Dedicated (customer-dedicated pools):
  - RTO: best-effort failover sequencing is 15-60 minutes depending on pool size and pre-warmed capacity; customers can purchase reserved cross-region standby to guarantee sub-15m restoration.
  - RPO: snapshot-based state (if used) has configurable frequency; with cross-region replication enabled, practical RPO is under 1 minute for critical state.

Failover sequencing (overview):
1) Detection & trigger: automated health checks + ops pager -> failover trigger (0s–2m)
2) Control-plane reconfiguration: promotion of secondary region instance and routing policy update (1–5m)
3) Traffic shift: DNS + edge routing short TTL (~60s) to reduce cutover time (1–5m)
4) Data-plane warm-up: KV cache prefill and model warm-start (5–20m depending on model size)
5) Capacity ramp: autoscaling to target throughput; progressive traffic shifting to avoid overload (up to 30m)

Dependencies and gotchas:
- KMS keys: if customers use customer-managed KMS/HSM, ensure cross-region key availability; otherwise key rotation can delay cryptographic operations.
- Large model cold starts: very large models (hundreds of GB) benefit from pre-warmed standby; otherwise first-request latency can spike.
- Network quotas/peering: private deployments require preconfigured peering and firewall rules for fast failover.

Attached artifacts: Redwood_DR_Summary_20260722.pdf (summary of SLAs and test results), and an ops checklist excerpt (DR_Warmup_Steps.md) referenced in the email.

Next steps: if useful, Marcus can join a short technical call to review sequencing and warm-up timings with your infra/sec folks.

Best,
Grace O'Connor
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
+1 415-555-0123

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Meera Rao <meera@clearshield.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 23 Jul 2026 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: ClearShield RFP - failover sequencing detail

Meera — quick technical add from the runtime/ops side to expand the warm-up and sequencing bullets Grace shared:

- Warm-up strategy:
  - Model kernel preloading: we keep a small pool of warm model instances for common model families; for custom large models we recommend a pre-warm window or incremental traffic ramp.
  - KV cache prefill: for predictable workloads we support prefix caching from snapshot buckets; prefill time is proportional to cache volume but typically completes in 3–10 minutes for small-to-medium caches.
- DNS & edge propagation:
  - We use an edge routing layer plus short DNS TTLs (60s) to ensure fast cutover; we also maintain health probes at multiple CDNs to accelerate failover.
- Verification & smoke tests:
  - After traffic shift we execute a short test-suite (functional + latency checks) and only continue ramp if thresholds pass. This is typically a 2–5 minute window.

Operational note: we run quarterly tabletop DR exercises with a subset of customers; documented outcomes and redacted test artifacts are included in the attached PDF. Happy to provide a signed attestation of the exercise cadence.

-Marcus
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference

[Attachment referenced: DR_Warmup_Steps.md]

Grace / Marcus —

Thanks for the fast, thorough responses and the attachments. A few follow-ups before we close this packet:

- Can you provide a short, signed attestation (one page) that describes your quarterly DR exercises and that you will provide redacted summaries on request?
- Please confirm whether SOC2 Type II report and recent pen-test summary (redacted) are available under NDA; if so, include the process to obtain them (DocuSign/NDA link or security portal).
- We need a clear statement on maximum accepted RTO for Dedicated pools without purchased standby capacity (please put a single max number we can bind to contract).

If you can drop the attestation and SOC2 access instructions by Thurs EOD our procurement team can move the RFP to the contract stage. Also propose a 30-minute call next Tuesday to finalize a short mutual action plan.

Best,
Meera Rao
Director, Vendor Security
ClearShield Financial
